Vikas Bahl, J. (Oral)
1.

Challenge in the present appeal is to the judgment dated 08.01.2000, vide which the claim petition filed by respondents No.1 to 3, who are the widow and parents of the deceased, Amar Singh alias Rattan Lal, filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, has been allowed and a compensation of Rs.2,50,400/- alongwith interest has been awarded to the claimants.
National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Smt. Nirmala Devi on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95468175/

sentences.text: Present appeal has been filed by the appellant-Insurance Company which has been impleaded as respondent No.4 in the claim petition.

Krishan Kumar-respondent No.4 is the driver of the offending 1 of 12 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:170269 truck, respondent No.5/Gurbachan Singh and respondent No.6/S.K. Chaudhary are the joint owners of the offending truck.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company has submitted that in the present case, the Tata truck bearing registration No.DHG 145, which is stated to be the offending truck, was not involved in the accident and the said fact is apparent from the fact that the FIR No.318 dated 28.08.1994, registered under Sections 279, 336 and 337 IPC (Section 304-A IPC added later on), at Police Station City Sirsa, did not mention the number of the said truck.
It is further submitted that RW-1 Gopal Krishan, Head Constable, has stated in his evidence that the criminal case has been filed as being untraced, vide report dated 07.01.1995.

It is argued that from the said facts, it is apparent that the truck in question was never involved in the accident and thus, the question of the present appellant, the insurer of the said truck, being liable does not arise and the impugned award qua the present appellant deserves to be set aside on the said ground alone and the present appeal deserves to be allowed.
4. Learned counsel appearing for respondents No.1 to 3, who are the contesting respondents in the present case, has opposed the present appeal and has submitted that the factum of the accident having taken place with the truck in question is proved beyond doubt from the pleadings of the parties as well as from the evidence of the eye witness Subhash Chander, who has been examined as PW-1 and nothing has been shown from his cross-examination to even remotely dislodge his 2 of 12 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:170269 evidence.

It is stated that in the present case, the stand taken by the driver as well as the joint owners of the truck in question was to the effect that it was the fault of the deceased and the said eye witness, inasmuch as, when the driver of the offending vehicle tried to overtake the cycle on which the deceased and the eye witness Subhash Chander were travelling, the said persons lost the balance of the cycle which struck on the side of the truck on account of which Amar Singh alias Rattan Lal died.

It is further stated that a perusal of the said statement would show that the said driver and owners had admitted that the accident took place with the truck in question but they had tried to attribute negligence to the deceased and the eye witness Subhash Chander.
It is submitted that the said driver has not been examined by the present appellant and thus, there is no rebuttal to the version given by the eye witness Subhash Chander in his evidence as PW-1.
It is further submitted that the finding of the Tribunal is based on the pleadings and the evidence on record and does not call for any interference and the instant appeal deserves to be dismissed.

It is stated that the amount of compensation awarded has already been released to the claimants and in case of any interference of this Court in the said award, then, the same would result in irreparable loss to the claimants.
5. This Court has heard learned counsel for the parties and has perused the paperbook as well as the record of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal.

6. Before referring to the facts of the present case, it would be relevant to mention that it is not disputed before this Court that the 3 of 12 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:170269 amount of compensation awarded vide award dated 08.01.2000 has already been released to the claimants by National Insurance Co. sentences.text:
the Insurance Company/present appellant and the claimants in the present case are the widow and the parents of the deceased Amar Singh alias Rattan Lal, who had died in the accident that had taken place on 27.08.1994 with the offending Tata truck bearing registration No.DHG 145.
7.

Brief facts of the case are that respondents No.1 to 3 had filed a claim petition for grant of compensation to the tune of Rs.10,00,000/- under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, as amended upto date, on account of the death of Amar Singh alias Rattan Lal, which had taken place due to the accident which had occurred on 27.08.1994.

In the claim petition, it was the case of the claimants that on 27.08.1994 at about 9.30 PM, the deceased Amar Singh alias Rattan Lal alongwith eye witness Subhash Chander son of Vasudev and Devki Nandan were coming on a cycle from Mohalla Gau Shala, after taking dinner from the house of Parlhad son of Hari Ram and were going to the house of Surja Ram and when they had reached near Surkhab Chowk, Sirsa, to turn towards old Court, a Tata truck bearing registration No.DHG-145 which was being driven by Krishan Kumar at a very high speed and in a very rash and negligent manner and without blowing any horn struck into the cycle of the deceased from the back side in its attempt to overtake the cycle.

It was stated that the said truck was coming from Dabwali side and on account of the said accident, the deceased had suffered multiple serious and grievous injuries and was admitted to General Hospital, Sirsa 4 of 12 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:170269 by the other occupants of the cycle, who had witnessed the said accident.

It was further stated that the deceased was referred to M.C.H. Rohtak on 28.08.1994 and since the concerned Neuro Surgeon was at Gulati Nursing Home at Hisar, therefore,
he was admitted to Gulati Nursing Home at Hisar, where he remained an indoor patient for about one and a half month and since the the injuries proved to be fatal, he succumbed to the said injuries.

It was stated that the driver Krishan Kumar had run away with the offending vehicle from the spot but however after 2-3 days of the accident, the said Krishan Kumar alongwith the owners of the offending vehicle i.e. Gurbachan Singh and S.K. Chaudhary had come to Gulati Nursing Home at Hisar and had apologised for causing the accident.

It was specifically stated that the accident had taken place on account of rash and negligent driving of respondent No.1 Krishan Kumar, who was working under the employment of said Gurbachan Singh and S.K. Chaudhary.

8. The written statement was filed on behalf of Krishan Kumar, Gurbachan Singh and S.K.
Chaudhary, who were the driver and the joint owners of the truck in question and in para 24 of the written statement, the fact that the accident had taken place with the truck in question was not disputed but the said respondents had taken a plea that when the driver of the truck was trying to overtake the cycle, it was the cyclist who lost the balance and struck the cycle on the side of the truck.

The fact that the said respondents had gone to the Hospital to meet the injured and had told them the real facts of the accident, was not disputed and rather, was 5 of 12 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:170269 admitted.
9. The Insurance Company had filed a separate written statement and had opposed the claim petition.

10. The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sirsa, framed the following issues, which arose from the pleadings: -

sentences.text: 1. Whether Amar Singh alias Rattan Lal died as a result of injuries received by him in motor vehicular accident which took place on 27.8.1994 in the area of City Sirsa on account of rash and negligent driving of Truck No. DHG 145 by respondent Krishan Kumar?

OPP. 
2. Whether petitioners are legal heirs/dependents of deceased Amar Singh alias Rattan Lal?

OPP. 
3. How much amount of compensation petitioners are entitled to receive compensation and from whom?

OPP. 
4. Whether respondent no.4 is not liable for the reasons and grounds stated in its written statement?OPR 5. Relief."
11. After taking into consideration the entire evidence as well as the documents on record, the Tribunal decided Issue No.1 in favour of the claimants and against the respondents.
Under the said issue, the Tribunal took into consideration the evidence of PW-1 Subhash Chander, who was an eye witness and who had fully supported the case of the claimants.

The evidence of the said witness to the effect that the truck driver Krishan Kumar had also come to the hospital where the deceased was admitted and he was identified by him was taken into consideration and it was noticed that the said evidence of Subhash Chander (PW1) had gone unrebutted and the fact that the said Gurbachan Singh and S.K. 6 of 12 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:170269 Chaudhary were the registered owners of the vehicle in question was not disputed.

It was also observed that in the written statement filed by the driver and the joint owners, the fact of the accident having taken place with the truck in question was not disputed and with respect to the version put-forth by the driver and the joint owners, there was no evidence and that even the driver had not been examined.

12. The plea sought to be raised by Gurbachan Singh while appearing as RW-3 to the effect that he had not signed the said written statement and had not engaged Mr. B.S. Saini, Advocate, on his behalf, was rejected after taking into consideration the power of attorney which had been placed at page No.75 of the Tribunal's file on which all the three respondents had signed the Vakalatnama and it was noticed by the Tribunal that the respondent Gurbachan Singh while appearing as RW-3 did not even utter a word that the said Vakalatnam was not signed by him.

It was also observed that even the signatures of Gurbachan Singh on the written statement and power of attorney were not got compared with his specimen signatures from any Handwriting and Finger Print Expert and even Krishan Kumar, driver of the offending vehicle and S.K. Chaudhary, co-owner of the truck, had not been examined to deny that they had not filed any written statement or that they had not engaged Mr. B.S. Saini, Advocate as a counsel.
Moreover, at any rate, neither the driver nor the co-owner of the truck in question had filed an appeal to challenge the finding of the Tribunal on the said aspect.

On the basis of the same, it was found by the Tribunal that Amar Singh alias Rattan Lal had died as a 7 of 12 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:170269 result of injuries received by him in a motor vehicular accident which took place on 27.08.1994 on account of rash and negligent driving of the National Insurance Co. sentences.text: 13. Under Issue No.2, the Tribunal found that the claimants were fully dependent on the deceased and were thus entitled to file the claim petition and the said issue was also decided in favour of the claimants and against the respondents.

14. Under Issues No.3 and 4, the Tribunal took into consideration the fact that the deceased was to be treated as a skilled labourer and it was thus presumed that his earning would be about Rs.1800/-
per month as he knew embroidery and after making the deduction of 1/3rd of the amount which the deceased would be spending on himself out of his income, found the dependency to be Rs.1200/-
per month or Rs.14400/- per year and by applying the multiplier of '16', had assessed the amount of compensation to be Rs.2,30,400/- and had further found that an amount of Rs.20,000/- would have been spent by him on the treatment before he succumbed to the injuries and thus, the total compensation which the claimants were found entitled to was Rs.2,50,400/-.

Respondent No.1 as well as respondent Nos.2 and 3 were found jointly as well as severally liable and it was further observed that it was the primary responsibility of respondent No.4, which was the Insurance Company, to pay the said amount to the claimants.

The findings on Issues No.2, 3 and 4 have not been challenged before this Court and at 8 of 12 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:170269 any rate,
the said findings are in accordance with law and deserve to be upheld.

15. With respect to the arguments raised by learned counsel for the appellant to the effect that the truck in question was not involved in the accident and the finding on Issue No.1 deserves to be reversed, it would be relevant to note that in the present case, the details of the accident have been given in the claim petition.

The relevant portion of para 24 of the claim petition is reproduced herein below: -
"24.
That on 27.8.94. at about 9.30. P.M. the deceased Amar @ Rattan Lal, alongwith Subhash Chander s/o sh. Vasu Dev caste Kaushik and Devki Nandan s/o Sh.

Satnarain caste Mallajan, both the r/o Mohalla Gau Shala, Sirsa was coming on a cycle from Mohalla Gau Shala, After taking dinner from the house of Prahllad s/o sh.
Hari Ram caste Mahajan and was going to Dhani Surja Ram i.e. in Laws of the deceased Amar Singh @Rattan Lal which is situated in the back side of the H.S.E.B.
Office Sirsa, when they reached near the Surkhab Chowk to turn towards old Court, a Tata Truck bearing regd. No. DHG-145 which was driven by Respondent No 1, i.e.
Krishan Kumar in a very high speed rashly negligent, in a zig-zag manner, without blowing any horn and abiding by necessary traffic rules come from the Dabwali side and struck into the cycle of the deceased from back side in process to cross the cycle.

Due to this accident the deceased and other received injuries, but, the deceased received multiple serious and grievous injuries on his person and was admitted to Gernal Hospital Sirsa by other occupants of the cycle who also witness this accident from his eyes.
The deceased was referred to M.C.H. Rohtak on 28.7.94.
but, the Neuro Surgeon Dr. S.K. Dua Neuro Sergeon M. C.H. Rohtak was at Gulati Nursing Home at Hisar on his weekly visit.

Therefore, he was admitted to Gulati Nursing Home at Hisar where he remained an indoor patient for about one and half month,

sentences.text: later on, the 9 of 12 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:170269 injuries prove fatal and he succumbed due to the injuries.
The Respondent No 1, i.e. Krishan Kumar run away with offending vehicle Tata Truck from the spot.

On the next day of accident i.e.
on 28.8.94. the police came to the General Hospital, Sirsa alongwith respondent No 1, and others.
At that time, the respondent No 1, i.e. Krishan Kumar made apologies for causing this accident.

However, after 2/3 days of this accident the respondent No 1, alongwith the owners of the offending vehicle i.e. respondent No 2 & 3 came ame to Gulati Nursing Home at Hisar and made apologies for causing this accident.
xxx xxx xxx

This accident took place purely and exclusively due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent No 1, i.e. Krishan Kumar who was working under the employment of respondent No 2 & 3, At that time, and all the respondents for jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation as prayed for."

16. A perusal of the above would show that it has been specifically pleaded by the claimants that the accident had taken place on account of the rash and negligent driving of Krishan Kumar, who was the driver of the Tata Truck and that the said driver as well as the joint owners of the offending truck had come to meet the deceased in the hospital and had apologised.
17.
In the written statement filed by the driver and the joint owners, the fact of the accident having taken place with the truck in question had not been disputed.
Even the fact that the said three persons had gone to the hospital to meet the injured/deceased has been admitted.
Thus, the involvement of the truck in question is prima facie established from the pleadings of the parties itself.

The plea of rash and negligent 10 of 12 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:170269 driving of the said Krishan Kumar has however not been admitted by the said three persons and rather, a case has been built up that when the said Krishan Kumar had tried to overtake the cycle, it was the deceased who had lost the balance and had struck the cycle on the side of the truck.
The said plea could not be established during the trial as no supporting evidence was led on behalf of the respondents.
The driver of the truck did not step into the witness box and Gurbachan Singh (co-owner), who was examined as RW-1, was admittedly not an eye witness to the occurrence.

The star witness Subhash Chander who was an eye witness in the present case was examined as PW-1 and in his evidence, he had fully supported the case of the claimants as had been stated in the claim petition and nothing has been shown from his cross-examination to this Court to dislodge the evidence given by the said witness in his examination-in- chief.

Thus, the testimony of PW-1 Subhash Chander who was the eye witness had gone unrebutted and the Tribunal has rightly relied upon the said testimony and other evidence and accordingly has rightly decided Issue No.1 in favour of the claimants.

18. Before parting, it would be relevant to note that earlier, the appeal filed by the Insurance Company was allowed by a Co-ordinate Bench of this Court and the said order was set aside by the Hon'ble Supreme Court and the case was remanded back for fresh consideration in accordance with law.

6 19. Keeping in view the above-said facts and circumstances, this Court is of the view that the impugned award has been correctly passed 11 of 12 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:170269 and deserves to be upheld and the present appeal filed by the appellant- Insurance Company being meritless, deserves to be dismissed and is accordingly dismissed.
